mechanisms.evidence_quote:
the definition of system boundaries
and assumptions used for the evaluation often vary which hinders the
comparison of SECs taken from different studies.

One of the difficulties
occurs for integrated processes as a clear allocation of the energy
consumption to specific production steps or products is not possible.

The
contributors to this deviation are not identified by the model and thus are
unknown unless additional process knowledge is incorporated.

One es-
sential requirement for the evaluation is the correction of these indicators and the corresponding baselines by the
influences of external static or dynamic factors, e.g. the ambient conditions, the product spectrum or the plant
load.

It
has been shown that seasonal effects, e.g. the utilization or the ambient
temperature, can have a strong impact on the absolute value of the
energy intensity of an integrated production site

The energy consumption of a single product in a multi-product
process can only be determined by incorporating additional process
knowledge.

reviewer_notes: This is primarily a methodology paper proposing a hierarchical aggregation method for EnPIs/EnBs, demonstrated on a semi-synthetic example (numerical values modified for confidentiality) based on the INEOS Cologne petrochemical site. M1 is the aggregated site-level EnPI/BDP model; M2–M4 are the plant-level Best-Demonstrated-Practice baseline models (ammonia, acrylonitrile, propylene oxide). Each plant model carries three energy-carrier equations (steam, electricity, natural gas); these were kept as one model per plant rather than split per carrier. Plant baseline equations are given in Appendix A but the payload text is heavily garbled, so functional form (linear for NH3; quadratic terms for AN and POX) and the P>0 validity domain are recorded with requires-inference support. The event-triggered re-estimation regime reflects the paper's stated capability to adapt baselines on process modification; it is recorded as proposed since no coefficient re-estimation is shown in the example.
